title: What's in a Name?: Counting, Tally Marks and Data
seo_title: Counting, Tally Marks and Data Class 3 Worksheet with Answers (Maths Mela Chapter 1)
standard_code: Class 3, Maths Mela Chapter 1: What's in a Name?
standard_text: Counting objects and letters, recording counts with tally marks, organising them in tables and comparing them (summary of NCERT Maths Mela Class 3)
meta_desc: Class 3 What's in a Name? worksheet (Maths Mela Chapter 1): counting with tally marks, tally tables, pictographs and comparing. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Tally marks are drawn in fives.
key_sub: Count the groups of five, then the extra marks.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Tally marks: four lines and one across = 5.
  • Count tallies in fives, then add the rest: two fives and 3 = 13.
  • A table lets us compare: which is most, fewest, how many more.

Examples

Example

Count: two groups of five and 4 more.

5 + 5 + 4

Answer: 14

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting the crossing line as a sixth markFour upright lines and one across make 5.
Adding when asked how many moreHow many more means subtract.

faq.q: Why is the chapter called What's in a Name?
faq.a: Children count letters in names and record the counts with tally marks.
Marks drawn in groups of five to keep count quickly.

items.q: What number do these tally marks show?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. Count the groups in 5s, then count on the single marks: 1 group of 5 and 3 more: 1 × 5 = 5, and 5 + 3 = 8.

items.q: What number do these tally marks show?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. Count the groups in 5s, then count on the single marks: 2 groups of 5 and 3 more: 2 × 5 = 10, and 10 + 3 = 13.

items.q: What number do these tally marks show?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. Count the groups in 5s, then count on the single marks: 3 groups of 5 and 4 more: 3 × 5 = 15, and 15 + 4 = 19.

items.q: What number do these tally marks show?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. Count the groups in 5s, then count on the single marks: 4 groups of 5 and 2 more: 4 × 5 = 20, and 20 + 2 = 22.
16 = 5 + 5 + 5 + 1, so look for 3 groups of 5 and 1 single mark. That is C. A shows 21 (one group of 5 too many); B shows 15 (one single mark is missing); D shows 17 (one single mark too many).

items.q: How many families have 4 people?
items.e: Find the row for 4 people. The frequency is 10 (2 groups of 5). The 4 is the number of people, not the number of families.

items.q: What is the most common family size?
items.e: The biggest frequency is 10, in the row for 4 people. So 4 people is the most common family size. 10 is how many families, not how many people.

items.q: How many families are in the survey?
items.e: Add the frequencies: 3 + 8 + 10 + 5 + 2 = 28 families. (20 is 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6, the family sizes.)

items.q: How many families have more than 4 people?
items.e: More than 4 means 5 or 6 people: 5 + 2 = 7 families. Do not include the families with exactly 4 people. (17 adds the 4-people row too.)

items.q: How many more chickadees than cardinals were seen?
items.e: Chickadee 12, cardinal 8. How many more means subtract: 12 − 8 = 4.

items.q: What number do these tally marks show?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. Count the groups by 5s, then count on the single marks. 1 group of 5, then 2 more: 5, then 6, 7. So 7. (6 counts each group as 4. Count the line across too.)

items.q: What number do these tally marks show?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. Count the groups by 5s, then count on the single marks. 2 groups of 5, then 2 more: 5, 10, then 11, 12. So 12. (10 counts each group as 4. Count the line across too.)

items.q: What number do these tally marks show?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. Count the groups by 5s, then count on the single marks. 1 group of 5, then 4 more: 5, then 6, 7, 8, 9. So 9. (8 counts each group as 4. Count the line across too.)

items.q: What number do these tally marks show?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. Count the groups by 5s, then count on the single marks. 3 groups of 5, then 1 more: 5, 10, 15, then 16. So 16. (13 counts each group as 4. Count the line across too.)
13 = 5 + 5 + 3, so look for 2 groups of 5 and 3 single marks. That is C. A shows 12 (one mark too few), B shows 18 (one group of 5 too many) and D shows 14 (one mark too many).

items.q: What number should go in the Total column for Football?
items.e: Football has 2 groups of 5, then 1 more: 5, 10, then 11. So 11. (9 counts the group of 5 as 4 marks.)

items.q: How many students chose hockey?
items.e: Find the Hockey row. The tally shows 1 group of 5, then 3 more: 5, then 6, 7, 8. So 8. Do not read the Kabaddi row below it (4).

items.q: Which sport did the fewest students choose?
items.e: Kabaddi has only 4 single marks. Every other sport has at least one group of 5.

items.q: How many more students chose hockey than swimming?
items.e: Hockey 8, swimming 7. How many more means find the difference: 8 − 7 = 1. (15 adds them instead.)

items.q: Every student voted once. How many students voted?
items.e: Football 11, hockey 8, kabaddi 4, swimming 7, basketball 6. 11 + 8 + 4 + 7 + 6 = 36. (25 leaves out football, the row with the ?. 31 counts each group of 5 as 4.)

items.q: How many votes did Pear get?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. The Pear row has 2 groups of 5 and 4 more: 2 × 5 = 10, and 10 + 4 = 14.

items.q: How many votes did Apple get?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. The Apple row has 3 groups of 5 and 2 more: 3 × 5 = 15, and 15 + 2 = 17.

items.q: How many students chose cricket?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. The Cricket row has 1 group of 5 and 1 more: 1 × 5 = 5, and 5 + 1 = 6.

items.q: Which row shows 17 students?
items.e: 17 = 5 + 5 + 5 + 2. Look for 3 groups of 5 and 2 single marks. That is the Netball row.

items.q: How many white cars were there?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. The White row has 3 groups of 5 and 2 more: 3 × 5 = 15, and 15 + 2 = 17.

items.q: How many cars are shown in the tally chart altogether?
items.e: Count each row: Black 7, White 17, Silver 10, Red 9. Then add: 7 + 17 + 10 + 9 = 43 cars.

items.q: How many buses went past the school?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. The Bus row has 1 group of 5 and 4 more: 1 × 5 = 5, and 5 + 4 = 9.

items.q: What is the difference between the biggest and the smallest number of vehicles?
items.e: The biggest is Lorry (12). The smallest is Van (4). Difference means subtract: 12 − 4 = 8.

items.q: Which row shows 16 small creatures?
items.e: 16 = 5 + 5 + 5 + 1. Look for 3 groups of 5 and 1 single mark. That is the Worm row.

items.q: How many small creatures are shown in the tally chart altogether?
items.e: Count each row: Ladybird 13, Worm 16, Snail 9, Spider 10. Then add: 13 + 16 + 9 + 10 = 48 small creatures.

items.q: How many spiders did class 3A find?
items.e: Find the Spiders row, then go across to the Class 3A column. The cell says 11.

items.q: How many more snails did class 3A find than class 3B?
items.e: How many more means find the difference: 16 − 12 = 4.

items.q: Which small creature did the two classes find the most of altogether?
items.e: Add each row: Ladybirds 9 + 14 = 23, Worms 17 + 8 = 25, Snails 16 + 12 = 28, Spiders 11 + 3 = 14. The biggest total is 28, for snails.

items.q: How many books did Tara read in week 2?
items.e: Find the Tara row, then go across to the Week 2 column. The cell says 8.

items.q: How many books did the four students read in week 2?
items.e: Add the whole Week 2 column: 3 + 13 + 10 + 8 = 34.

items.q: How many more books did Ishaan read in week 1 than in week 2?
items.e: How many more means find the difference: 12 − 3 = 9.

items.q: How many students had a hot dinner on Monday?
items.e: Find the Monday row, then go across to the Hot dinner column. The cell says 17.

items.q: How many students had lunch on Thursday altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. Add the two cells in the Thursday row: 16 + 11 = 27.

items.q: How many students had a hot dinner from Monday to Thursday?
items.e: Add the whole Hot dinner column: 17 + 24 + 23 + 16 = 80.

items.q: How many cars went past the school?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. The Car row has 1 group of 5 and 1 more: 1 × 5 = 5, and 5 + 1 = 6.

items.q: How many galahs were seen?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle stands for 1 bird. The Galah row has 7 circles, so it shows 7 birds.
Every star stands for the same number, so the row with the most stars shows the most. The Gauri row has 7 stars, so it shows 7 shells.

items.q: How many more students have a guinea pig than a cat?
items.e: Look at the key: each square stands for 1 student. Guinea pig: 5 and Cat: 3. How many more means find the difference: 5 − 3 = 2 students.

items.q: How many students chose cricket?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle stands for 1 student. The Cricket row has 4 circles, so it shows 4 students.
Look at the key: each star stands for 1 vote. Read every row: Watermelon 5, Banana 3, Apple 6, Mango 8. Add them: 5 + 3 + 6 + 8 = 22 votes.

items.q: How many ice blocks were sold on Monday?
items.e: Look at the key: each square stands for 2 ice blocks. The Mon row has 2 squares: 2 × 2 = 4 ice blocks.
The key says one whole star = 2 students. Half a star is half of 2, which is 1 student.

items.q: Each star stands for 2 books. Nikhil read 12 books. How many stars should be in his row?
items.e: Count in 2s until you reach 12: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. That is 6 steps, so draw 6 stars. Check: 6 × 2 = 12. (Drawing 12 stars would show 12 × 2.)

items.q: Which row shows 5 books?
items.e: Half a circle is 1, so 5 books is 2 and a half circles. The Ishaan row has 2 circles and half a circle: 2 × 2 = 4, and half of 2 is 1, so 4 + 1 = 5 books.
Look at the key: each star stands for 2 students. The AFL row has 5 stars and half a star: 5 × 2 = 10, and half of 2 is 1, so 10 + 1 = 11 students.

items.q: How many apples did Diya pick?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle stands for 2 apples. The Diya row has 5 circles: 5 × 2 = 10 apples. (5 apples would mean each circle is 1.)
Every star stands for the same number, so the row with the most stars shows the most. The Rehan row has 6 stars: 6 × 2 = 12 books.

items.q: Which row shows 7 students?
items.e: Half a circle is 1. The Bike row has 3 circles and half a circle: 3 × 2 = 6, and half of 2 is 1, so 6 + 1 = 7 students.

items.q: Each star stands for 2 books. Priya read 14 books. How many stars should be in her row?
items.e: Count by 2s until you reach 14: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. That is 7 steps, so draw 7 stars. Check: 7 × 2 = 14. (Drawing 14 stars would mean each star stands for 1.)

items.q: How many more cardinals than sparrows were seen?
items.e: Look at the key: each square stands for 2 birds. Cardinal: 5 × 2 = 10. Sparrow: 2 × 2 = 4. How many more means find the difference: 10 − 4 = 6 birds. (3 is the difference in symbols, not in birds.)
Look at the key: each star stands for 5 laps. The Class 2 row has 4 stars: 4 × 5 = 20 laps. (4 laps would mean each star is 1.)

items.q: Which row shows 25 hot chocolates?
items.e: Each square = 5. 25 ÷ 5 = 5, so look for 5 squares. The Tue row has 5 squares: 5 × 5 = 25 hot chocolates.

items.q: Each square stands for 5 students. 30 students walk to school. How many squares should be in the Walk row?
items.e: Count by 5s until you reach 30: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. That is 6 steps, so draw 6 squares. Check: 6 × 5 = 30. (Drawing 30 squares would mean each square stands for 1.)
Look at the key: each star stands for 5 cans. The Mr. Khan row has 7 stars: 7 × 5 = 35 cans. (7 cans would mean each star is 1.)

items.q: How many more apples did Arjun pick than Nikhil?
items.e: Look at the key: each square stands for 5 apples. Arjun: 7 × 5 = 35. Nikhil: 4 × 5 = 20. How many more means find the difference: 35 − 20 = 15 apples. (3 is the difference in symbols, not in apples.)

items.q: How many more students have a dog than a rabbit?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. Dog 8 and Rabbit 3. How many more means find the difference: 8 − 3 = 5 students.
Each star = 5. Banana 6 × 5 = 30 and Pear 4 × 5 = 20. Altogether means add: 30 + 20 = 50 votes.

items.q: How many fewer cans did class 3C collect than 3A?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. 3A 60 and 3C 50. How many fewer means find the difference: 60 − 50 = 10 cans.

items.q: How many blackbirds and sparrows were seen altogether?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. Blackbird 15 and Sparrow 25. Altogether means add: 15 + 25 = 40 birds.

items.q: How many fewer students walk to school than come by scooter?
items.e: Each square = 10, so half a square = 5. Scooter 3 × 10 = 30 and Walk 1 × 10 = 10. How many fewer means find the difference: 30 − 10 = 20 students.

items.q: How many students voted altogether?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. Read every bar: Football 5, Netball 11, Cricket 12, Swimming 10. Add them: 5 + 11 + 12 + 10 = 38 students.

items.q: How many more mystery books than animal books were borrowed?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. Mystery 30 and Animals 10. How many more means find the difference: 30 − 10 = 20 books.

items.q: How many points did Kestrel and Owl get altogether?
items.e: Each square = 10, so half a square = 5. Kestrel 5 × 10 = 50 and Owl 2 × 10 = 20. Altogether means add: 50 + 20 = 70 points.

items.q: How many fewer votes did Red get than Purple?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. Purple 7 and Red 2. How many fewer means find the difference: 7 − 2 = 5 votes.

items.q: How many more shells did Nikhil find than Rehan and Priya together?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. Nikhil 25, Rehan 5 and Priya 10. Step 1: Rehan and Priya together: 5 + 10 = 15. Step 2: 25 − 15 = 10 shells.

items.q: How many more laps did Gauri run than Neha?
items.e: Gauri: 8. Neha: 2. How many more means find the difference: 8 − 2 = 6. (10 adds instead of subtracting.)

items.q: How many fewer herons than ducks were seen?
items.e: Duck: 7. Heron: 1. How many fewer means find the difference: 7 − 1 = 6. (8 adds instead of subtracting.)

items.q: How many students chose basketball or hockey?
items.e: Basketball: 10. Hockey: 7. Altogether means add: 10 + 7 = 17.

items.q: How many students voted altogether?
items.e: Read every row: Peach: 8, Apple: 2, Cherry: 5, Pear: 3. Add them all: 8 + 2 + 5 + 3 = 18. Make sure you add every row once.

items.q: How many students walk or ride a bike to school?
items.e: Walk: 5. Bike: 8. Altogether means add: 5 + 8 = 13.

items.q: How many fewer cans did Mr. Gill’s class collect than Mr. Chen’s class?
items.e: Mr. Chen: 15. Mr. Gill: 4. How many fewer means find the difference: 15 − 4 = 11. (19 adds instead of subtracting.)

items.q: How many more books does the tallest bar show than the shortest bar?
items.e: The tallest bar is Rehan (10). The shortest is Meera (1). 10 − 1 = 9.

items.q: Every student is counted once. How many students did not choose pears?
items.e: Total: 1 + 3 + 7 + 4 = 15. Take away Pear (4): 15 − 4 = 11. You can also add the other rows: 1 + 3 + 7 = 11.

items.q: How many laps did Nikhil and Varun run altogether?
items.e: Nikhil: 19. Varun: 4. Altogether means add: 19 + 4 = 23.

items.q: How many more students does Car need to catch up to Bus?
items.e: Bus: 9. Car: 2. Count up from 2 to 9: that is 9 − 2 = 7 more. (9 is Bus’s number, not how many more.)

items.q: Favourite fruit: Apple 8, Pear 5, Plum 10, Kiwi 3. Which bar chart shows these numbers?
items.e: C matches every number (the scale goes up in 2s). A: two bars are the wrong way round; B: a bar is on the line below (it should be halfway between two lines); D: one bar is one line too high.

items.q: Minibeasts found: Ant 15, Worm 25, Snail 10, Slug 35. Which bar chart shows these numbers?
items.e: A matches every number (the scale goes up in 5s). B: two bars are the wrong way round; C: one bar is one line too high; D: one bar is one line too low.

items.q: Favourite colour: Red 40, Blue 25, Pink 60, Green 30. Which bar chart shows these numbers?
items.e: D matches every number (the scale goes up in 10s). A: two bars are the wrong way round; B: a bar is on the line below (it should be halfway between two lines); C: one bar is one line too high.
B matches every number (each symbol = 2). A: two rows are the wrong way round; C: a half symbol is drawn as a whole symbol; D: one row has a symbol too many.

items.q: Cakes sold: Mon 20, Tue 35, Wed 15, Thu 40. Which pictogram shows these numbers?
items.e: C matches every number (each symbol = 10). A: two rows are the wrong way round; B: a half symbol is drawn as a whole symbol; D: one row has a symbol too many.

items.q: Pets: Dog 15, Cat 10, Fish 20, Bird 5. Which pictogram shows these numbers?
items.e: A matches every number (each symbol = 5). B: two rows are the wrong way round; C: one row has a symbol too many; D: one row is missing a symbol.

items.q: Class 3 voted for their favourite fruit. How many more students chose grapes than pears?
items.e: Each circle = 2 votes, so half a circle = 1. Grapes: 5 × 2 = 10. Pear: 1 × 2 + 1 = 3. How many more means subtract: 10 − 3 = 7. (Half a circle is 1 here, because half of 2 is 1.)

items.q: How many more woodlice than snails did the class find?
items.e: Woodlice: 16. Snails: 6. How many more means subtract: 16 − 6 = 10. (5 is the number of grid spaces between the bars, not the number of small creatures.)
Each star = 5 books. Om has 5 stars: 5 × 5 = 25 books. 40 − 25 = 15 more books. (35 comes from counting the stars as 5 books.)
Kavya: 3 stars, 3 × 5 = 15. Tara: 2 stars, 2 × 5 = 10. Altogether: 15 + 10 = 25 books. (5 is the difference, or the number of stars.)

items.q: How many students chose AFL or football?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. AFL ends on 12. Football ends halfway between 8 and 10, so 9. AFL or football means add: 12 + 9 = 21. (Reading football as 8 gives 20.)

items.q: Every student in Class 3 voted once. How many students voted?
items.e: Read every column: 12, 7, 10, 9 and 4. Cricket and football end between gridlines, so they are 7 and 9. 12 + 7 + 10 + 9 + 4 = 42. (Reading 7 and 9 as 6 and 8 gives 40.)

items.q: How many pieces of fruit were eaten at recess altogether?
items.e: Each circle = 2, so half a circle = 1. Apple 8, banana 5 × 2 + 1 = 11, mango 6, orange 2 × 2 + 1 = 5. 8 + 11 + 6 + 5 = 30. (Counting the circles gives 16. Leaving out the halves gives 28.)

items.q: How many more bananas than oranges were eaten?
items.e: Banana 11, orange 5. How many more means subtract: 11 − 5 = 6. (3 is the difference in the number of circles, not in pieces of fruit.)

items.q: On which day were 15 more ice blocks sold than on Wednesday?
items.e: Wednesday: 10. 15 more than 10 is 10 + 15 = 25. Tuesday shows 25. (Monday shows 15, but the question asks for 15 more than Wednesday.)

items.q: On two days the weather was very hot. Which two days were most likely the hot days?
items.e: People buy more ice blocks on hot days. The two tallest columns are Thursday (35) and Friday (40).

items.q: How many students do not come to school by car?
items.e: Not by car means walk, bus or bike: 9 + 6 + 3 = 18. (32 is everyone, and 14 is only the car students.)

items.q: Next week 5 of the car students will walk instead. How many students will walk?
items.e: 5 more students will walk: 9 + 5 = 14. (19 adds the 5 to the car row instead.)

items.q: What is the most common number of people in a family?
items.e: The tallest column is above 4, so 4 people is the most common. The column is 8 high, which means 8 families, not 8 people.

items.q: How many families have 5 or more people?
items.e: 5 or more means the columns for 5 and 6 people: 4 + 2 = 6 families. (11 adds the family sizes 5 + 6, not the families.)
